name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 11 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Tim Kennedy has a large financial advantage ($2.3M raised, $1.2M on hand vs. minimal for Hannon)
Prediction markets price Kennedy at roughly 96% to win
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Kennedy: an 11-point Democratic lean, a favorable national environment, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge. Markets agree, pricing him near certain, so the forecast stays safely Democratic with a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Hannon within single digits, or a surge of Republican outside spending, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Kennedy, a first-term Democratic incumbent, seeks reelection in a Buffalo-area district that voted about eleven points more Democratic than the country in recent presidential elections. He faces Republican Dennis Hannon, a little-known challenger with no reported fundraising, while Kennedy has raised over $2.3 million and holds more than $1.2 million on hand. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have published ratings for the race.

Prediction markets give Kennedy roughly a 96% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals and the money gap. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with an expected margin of about twenty-one points and moderate uncertainty given the absence of polling.
